documents.unit: Center for Teaching Excellence (approved by Office of Academic Affairs)
documents.title: Syllabus Statements to Address the Usage of Artificial Intelligence in the Classroom
documents.stance_why: The page sets no university rule: 'Faculty are encouraged to add one of the three sample statements' and each sample begins 'For instructors who choose to' permit, limit or prohibit, so the decision is delegated and the three options are listed as tiers.
documents.summary: A Center for Teaching Excellence page offering three Academic Affairs-approved sample syllabus statements (permit with citation, limited use on select assignments, prohibit). Faculty choose one; the university sets no default and invites faculty to share their own statements.

units.why: The page tells faculty to add one of three Academic Affairs-approved sample statements; they are 'encouraged' but not required, so the phase is before-course and the modality 'should'. P09 fits best because it concerns stating AI expectations in the syllabus, though here it is encouraged rather than mandatory.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to add one of the three sample statements below to their syllabi
units.frag_start: Faculty are encouraged to add
units.frag_end: Office of Academic Affairs has approved.
units.fit_note: The statement is encouraged, not required; it is not mandatory in every syllabus.

units.why: Each sample begins 'For instructors who choose to' embrace, allow limited use of, or prohibit ChatGPT, and the page calls them 'suggested syllabus statements', so the choice among permitting, limiting or prohibiting is left to the instructor: P04. P05 does not fit because the options are samples for instructors, not tiers that students are placed in.

units.policy: Instructors choose among permitting, limiting or prohibiting ChatGPT or other AI generative software in their courses.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P04, actor=instructor, phase=before-course, modality=may. A's policy wording ('permitting, limiting or prohibiting') follows the three sample headings; B's added 'if any', which the page does not state, so A's wording is kept. Anchors differed but cover the same passage.

units.why: The page lists three Academic Affairs-approved sample statements headed 'EMBRACE/PERMIT', 'LIMITED/SELECT USAGE' and 'PROHIBIT/EXCLUDE'. These are named levels of AI use, so P05, addressed to faculty who pick one; they are samples for instructors, not tiers students are placed in.
units.anchor: EMBRACE/PERMIT
units.frag_start: Faculty are encouraged to add
units.frag_end: Office of Academic Affairs has approved.
units.policy: The university offers three approved sample syllabus statements: embrace/permit, limited/select usage, and prohibit/exclude.
units.fit_note: Options are sample statements for instructors, not tiers students are placed in.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P05, phase=before-course, modality=informs. They differed on actor: A instructor, B admin. The page is addressed to faculty ('Faculty are encouraged to add'), so the policy is addressed to instructors; instructor kept. Policy wording follows B (names the university and 'approved'), which the source supports. A's fit note kept.

units.why: The invitation to share statements and assignment language with CTE to 'build a repository' is a faculty-support and community mechanism, not a rule about student AI use; P63 fits since the CTE collects and supports instructors' policies.
units.anchor: faculty are invited to share their AI-related syllabus statements
units.frag_start: These are suggested syllabus statements
units.fit_note: Sharing builds a repository; no training or workshops are mentioned. Covers instructors sharing their statements to build a campus repository, not workshops or advice on learning AI.

units.why: The permit sample says ChatGPT 'may be used for any assignment with appropriate citation', a default permission with a citation condition, so permit with may, in the P02 default-permit category.
units.anchor: may be used for any assignment with appropriate citation
units.frag_start: Artificial intelligence (AI) language models, such as
units.policy: AI language models such as ChatGPT may be used for any assignment with appropriate citation.

units.why: The same permit statement requires 'appropriate citation' of AI use, a disclosure condition on the student. P24 is the right type as it is about acknowledging AI use in submissions; the permission itself is coded separately.
units.anchor: with appropriate citation
units.frag_start: may be used for any assignment
units.policy: AI use must be accompanied by appropriate citation.

units.why: 'You are responsible for fact-checking statements composed by AI Generative Software' puts verification on the student, matching P31 (verify AI output) rather than P29, because it is about checking accuracy of AI text.
units.anchor: You are responsible for fact-checking statements composed by AI Generative Software
units.frag_start: You are responsible for fact-checking
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on actor, phase, modality and P31. unit_stance: A permit, B neutral. The sentence 'You are responsible for fact-checking' sets a duty and takes no position on whether AI may be used, so neutral.

units.why: The permit sample opens by praising ChatGPT: it 'offers an innovative and effective approach to education, enhancing both teaching and learning'. It is a rationale for allowing AI as beneficial; P44 is the nearest type, with a fit note.
units.anchor: offers an innovative and effective approach to education, enhancing both teaching and learning experiences
units.frag_start: Integrating ChatGPT in the classroom offers
units.fit_note: Frames AI as beneficial to teaching and learning generally, not as a professional skill employers expect.

units.why: The limited sample says ChatGPT 'should be used selectively and thoughtfully', a soft norm to restrict use. P03 (discourage without forbidding) is chosen over P04 because it is a general cautious norm, not a decision about who sets the rule.
units.anchor: it should be used selectively and thoughtfully
units.frag_start: While ChatGPT presents valuable opportunities for
units.fit_note: Selective use is recommended as permitted in limited form; it is not framed as discouraging AI outright.

units.why: 'Limited usage of ChatGPT ensures that it serves as a supplementary tool rather than a replacement for human interaction' gives the reason for limiting use. P72 directs students to human help, which this does not do, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: serves as a supplementary tool rather than a replacement for human interaction
units.frag_start: Limited usage of ChatGPT ensures that it
units.uncovered_note: AI should supplement and not replace human interaction in teaching and learning.
units.resolution_why: A coded P72 with a fit note; B coded UNCOVERED. P72 covers directing students to instructors, librarians or other human support. The passage only says AI should supplement and not replace human interaction and directs no one anywhere, so the fit is stretched; per the codebook UNCOVERED is preferred. Actor, phase, modality and unit_stance agreed.

units.why: 'may be used on select assignments in this course, as defined by the instructor' permits AI only on assignments the instructor designates, so the rule is assignment-level and instructor-defined: P04. It is restrict because use is allowed only where designated.

units.why: The limited-usage sample repeats the duty 'You are responsible for fact-checking statements composed by AI Generative Software'. It sits in a different option, so it is coded again as P31 (verify AI output).

units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P31 and all other codes. unit_stance: A restrict, B neutral. As for the permit-sample copy, the sentence sets a verification duty and takes no position on AI use, so neutral. Kept as a separate unit because it appears in a different sample statement.

units.why: 'Intellectual honesty is vital to an academic community and for my fair evaluation of your work' opens the prohibit sample as a principle, not a rule. P56 is an institution-wide framework and this is one instructor's course statement, so it does not fit; UNCOVERED.

units.uncovered_note: Intellectual honesty is a value of the academic community and the basis for fair evaluation of student work, given as the reason for the prohibit option.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this sentence (as P56 with a fit note). It is a real statement in the source, so it is kept. P56 covers an institution-level framework, but the sentence is an instructor's course-level integrity rationale inside a sample statement, so the stretched fit is replaced by UNCOVERED per the codebook. Final: actor=all, phase=general, modality=informs, unit_stance=neutral.

units.why: 'The use of ChatGPT in this course is prohibited' bans use in the course outright, which is the default prohibition type P01 with must-not.

units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P29 and the other codes. unit_stance: A prohibit, B neutral. 'All work submitted in this course must be your own' does not mention AI, so on its own it takes no position on AI use; neutral.

units.why: 'All work submitted in this course must be your own and completed per the University's Administrative Guidelines on Academic Integrity' ties course work to existing university policy. P77 (comply with existing university policy) fits; P36 does not because no AI misuse is classified as misconduct and no process is named.
units.anchor: completed per the University’s Administrative Guidelines on Academic Integrity
units.frag_start: All work submitted in this course
units.policy: Work submitted in the course must be completed per the University's Administrative Guidelines on Academic Integrity.
units.resolution_why: A coded P77, phase=during-work; B coded P36, phase=general. P36 needs unauthorized AI use to be classified as misconduct and handled by integrity processes; this clause only requires work to follow the existing guidelines, which is P77. Phase: the clause governs how submitted work is completed, so during-work. Modality must (both).

units.why: 'You may not engage in unauthorized collaboration or use ChatGPT or other AI composition software' bans AI use in the course within the prohibit sample, so P01 with must-not. P06 does not fit because it defines what applies when a syllabus is silent, and this sample is an explicit ban.
units.anchor: You may not engage in unauthorized collaboration or use ChatGPT or other AI composition software.

units.fit_note: Bans unauthorized collaboration and AI use together in one sentence; the following sentence makes instructor permission the exception.
units.resolution_why: A coded P01; B coded P06 (permission-required fallback). The sentence is part of an explicit prohibit statement, not a rule for when the syllabus is silent, so P01. Actor, phase, modality (must-not) and unit_stance agreed.

units.why: 'Using these tools without my permission puts your academic integrity at risk' implies instructor permission can authorize use and that unauthorized use is an integrity issue. P36 fits as it links unauthorized AI use to academic integrity, though no process or sanction is stated.
